deities: Radha Raman (Krishna, self-manifested from a Shaligram Shila; no separate Radharani idol - a crown beside Krishna signifies her presence); Gopal Bhatta's other shaligram-shilas on the altar
festivals: Radha Raman Jayanti (Vaishakha Purnima - appearance day, milk abhisheka)

history.summary: One of the seven great Goswami temples of Vrindavan, established by Gopal Bhatta Goswami, disciple of Chaitanya Mahaprabhu. After Chaitanya's disappearance, Gopal Bhatta was instructed in a dream to visit Nepal; bathing in the Kali-Gandaki he received twelve Shaligram Shilas. On the Vaishakha full moon day (April-May) of 1542, one Shila self-manifested into the standing form of Radha Raman ('the one who gives pleasure to Radha') - an appearance celebrated annually with milk abhisheka. Radha Raman is one of the very few original Goswami deities still residing in Vrindavan (most were moved to Jaipur under Mughal threat). The temple keeps Chaitanya Mahaprabhu's kaupina and asana (brought by Gopal Bhatta from Jagannath Puri), shown publicly a few times a year; Gopal Bhatta's samadhi stands beside the appearance place, and the temple's kitchen fires are said to have burned continuously for over 435 years.

name: Radha Raman Temple
town_description: Vrindavan, on the Yamuna in Mathura district, Uttar Pradesh, is the sacred playground (leelasthali) of Krishna's youth and the heart of Braj bhumi. It hosts some of Hinduism's most beloved shrines - Banke Bihari, Radha Raman, Rangji, ISKCON's Krishna Balaram Mandir and Prem Mandir - and draws millions of pilgrims, especially for Holi and Janmashtami.

travel.road: Near Keshi Ghat road, old Vrindavan town, ~1 km east of the Banke Bihari Temple; narrow lanes - best reached on foot or by rickshaw from the main temple area

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Vaishakha Purnima (Radha Raman Jayanti) and Janmashtami for grandest celebrations; mornings and evenings for aartis
